{
  "research_brief": [
    "Current Approach 1: Smart storage hardware, such as ethylene absorbers and automated vacuum-sealers, designed to physically delay spoilage.",
    "Current Approach 2: In-home processing appliances, including countertop dehydrators and compact composters that turn scraps into usable inputs.",
    "Current Approach 3: AI-driven inventory software using computer vision or recipe engines to maximize use of existing pantry items.",
    "Failure 1: High user friction—manual logging apps show steep drop-off in active usage, as reported in consumer behavior studies.",
    "Failure 2: Energy offset—electric countertop appliances often consume significant power merely to dry food, shifting ecological impact to the energy grid.",
    "Criticism: Focusing primarily on household tech places systemic burden onto consumers while ignoring retail over-stocking and packaging incentives.",
    "Analogy: Passive HVAC climate control—just as smart thermostats auto-regulate temperature, food storage should dynamically adjust micro-humidity without manual setup."
  ]
}
